Occurrences.Kwic: 其僧一似韓獹逐塊。連忙上階。捉其月影相似。又問。如何是無寒暑處。山云。寒時寒殺闍黎。熱時熱殺闍黎。如韓獹逐塊走到階上。又却不見月影。韓獹乃出戰國策。云韓氏之獹駿狗也。中山之兔狡兔也。是其獹方能尋其兔。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). Yuanwu Keqin owns the exact clause in the complete case.

Senses.Explanation: “chasing the clod.” In the corpus it belongs to a recurrent animal comparison: “the lion bites the person; the hound chases the clod.” The phrase appears as an appraisal after exchanges and in admonitions such as “you must be a lion that bites the person; do not imitate the hound chasing the clod.” Related forms call people “mad dogs chasing the clod” and say “chasing the clod and tracking the scent does not yet make a good dog.” The hound and mad-dog variants share one literal image and one corpus deployment; they are not separate senses.
